**Answer: 2021**

The Scottish Mountain Rescue Statistics Report for 2021 is the only year between 2019‑2023 that satisfies all the requested criteria:

| Metric | 2019 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 |
|--------|------|------|------|------|
| Independent incidents | 502 | **660** | 636 | 572 |
| Separate team call‑outs | 672 | **893** | 843 | 870 |
| Volunteer hours | 26,934 | **31,799** | 29,804 | 32,762 |
| Fatalities | 14 | **19** | 21 | 41 |

- **Independent incidents** – 660 > 500 (2021)
- **Team call‑outs** – 893 > 800 (2021)
- **Volunteer hours** – 31,799 > 30,000 (2021)
- **Fatalities** – 19 < 25 (2021)

All other years either fall short on one or more of these thresholds.

**Sources**

- 2021 report: “The total number of independent incidents in 2021 was 660.” “The total number of separate team activations or ‘call‑outs’ was 893.” “Up 31,799 hours of their time during call‑outs.” “There were 19 fatalities…”. (PDF – *SMR Statistics Report 2021* – https://www.scottishmountainrescue.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/SMR_Statistics_Report_2021_v3_pages-FINAL.pdf)

- 2019 report (for comparison): “The total number of independent incidents in 2019 was 502.” “The total number of separate team callouts… was 672.” “Mountain Rescue team members gave 26,934 hours.” “There were 14 fatalities.” (PDF – *SMR Statistics Report 2019* – https://www.scottishmountainrescue.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/SMR_Statistics_Report_v3_Pages-2019-FINAL.pdf)
